title: UMG Inks Deal With ElevenLabs to Develop AI Music Remix Platform
key_facts: Universal Music Group signed a new multi-year licensing agreement with ElevenLabs, an AI audio company.
They will build a fan platform "built on licensed music and artist participation" to co-create, remix and mash up music from artists and songwriters who choose to take part.
Users can also render "personalized vocal experiences", and the companies will jointly develop AI audio products for artists and songwriters.
The deal does not cover ElevenMusic, ElevenLabs' music creation app, or its Music EPI models.
It comes a day after Suno launched v6, trained on music from UMG rivals WMG, Believe and BMG.
UMG and Sony Music are still pursuing a major lawsuit against Suno over alleged copyright infringement.
ElevenLabs has earlier music licensing deals with Merlin and Kobalt.
quote_evidence: Universal Music Group has inked a new multi-year licensing agreement with ElevenLabs, the AI audio research and product giant.
Importantly, this new deal with UMG is more about creating new products together, rather than partnering on ElevenLabs’ current music offerings.
Universal, alongside Sony Music, is still pursuing a major lawsuit against Suno over claims of widespread copyright infringement of their sound recordings
why_it_matters_hint: A major label licenses its catalogue for fan remixing with one AI company while suing another over copyright.
notes: Based on a press release with quotes from both chief executives; no launch date, pricing or payment terms given.
